title: The Wizard's Cabin
revision_notes: Rev 1.2 applies user-approved Blind Playtester recommendations R1 (feed-cup theory-magnet defused: ANY inventory item offered at the brass feed cup gets the same categorical terminal-refusal grammar as the cage reach -- new developer_notes D4; D1's block-or-allow decision for the DRAUGHT specifically is unchanged) and R2 (clock de-escalated: cuckoo-crow pops ONCE on first XII only, thereafter visibly inert with a limp broken spring; toy is clearly carved/paint-chipped, not an echo of the live crow -- new developer_notes D5; numeral ring untouched as p01 reference). Also records the playtest-calibrated blind-solve estimate (60-100 min). No puzzle, solution value, zone, or item changed.

Rev 1.1 applied Validator required fixes 1 & 2 (corrected example orderings; beam-at-alcove respecified as a latched derived CONDITION over moonbeam-on AND mirror-at-detent-3, not an event order) plus advisories A3 (brass feed cup as recognized mis-pour target), A6 (edge-list harmonization), and the p11 terminal-refusal annotation. No puzzle, solution value, zone, or item changed.
theme: Abandoned wizard's cabin deep in gloomy woods. Caged crow, potion-making, grimoire, arcane apparatus, hidden cellar.
framing_line: The wizard is gone. The crow remains.
time_of_day: Night, clear sky, visible moon and stars (required by puzzles p02, p03, p08-p10).

win_condition.description: Brew the Unbinding Draught, pour it into the front door's rune basin to wither the thorn-vine seal, then slide the bolt and exit.

derived_conditions.name: beam-at-alcove
derived_conditions.evaluation: Continuously evaluated boolean over two persistent latched states. TRUE the moment both inputs hold, REGARDLESS of the order in which the player achieved them (the mirror may be set to detent-3 before the shutter is ever cranked open, or after). Both inputs persist (no timers), so once true it stays true. This is a condition, never an event sequence. (Validator required fix 2.)

nodes.name: Silver coin stamped with a crescent
Phial of Unbinding Draught
nodes.notes: The brass feed cup (z1 cage) is a plausible mis-pour target -- see developer_notes D1. Cauldron remains draught-ready after filling, so a refill always exists.

nodes.content: Four element runes drawn beside pictograms: upward triangle + flame; downward triangle + wave; upward triangle with bar + cloud; downward triangle with bar + mountain. Maps pictogram to rune.
AIR rune scratched beside Roman numeral I.
FIRE rune scorched beside Roman numeral II.
EARTH rune beside Roman numeral III.
WATER rune beside Roman numeral IV.
Full Roman numeral ring I-XII; in-room reference for reading the numerals on the element marks. (Ring remains fully readable in all clock states, including the post-pop spent state -- R2.)
Three night paintings of the same tree. Painting with ONE crow: waxing crescent moon. TWO crows: full moon. THREE crows: waning gibbous moon. Crow count gives dial order; moon shape gives dial value.
Night sky with three bright stars in a short straight diagonal row (Orion's Belt) plus fainter surrounding stars matching the Orion plate's dot pattern.

Sun slot is a circular recess ringed with rays (fits the round gold ring); moon slot is a crescent recess (fits the crescent-stamped coin). Grimoire margin (page B) shows sun symbol beside a ring pictogram and crescent symbol beside a coin pictogram.

Pictographic recipe: moonflower blossom crushed in mortar; crescent-stamped metal filed into shavings; a black feather drawn floating INTO an open hand (freely given); flame pictogram with numeral III; spiral with arrowhead pointing counterclockwise and five dots along the spiral.
Scratch marks worn into the floor at the mirror's third detent position.

Reaching into the cage (for a feather or anything else) OR offering any inventory item at the brass feed cup triggers the SAME terminal refusal: the crow snaps once, then turns its back and guards its wing; any offered item returns to inventory unspent. Tone is categorical rejection ('this will never work'), NOT a near-miss 'try again' cue. Repeats replay the identical closed-off pose with no escalation or variation, signaling a dead interaction -- reaching in and feeding are BOTH non-paths (R1). Echoes the recipe's 'freely given' pictogram.

nodes.name: Workshop rune lock
nodes.mechanic: environmental-scavenger + symbol mapping + ordered code entry
nodes.input: Press four rune tiles in sequence.
nodes.derivation: Four element runes hidden around z1, each paired with a Roman numeral I-IV giving press order. Grimoire page A maps runes to element pictograms; mantel clock provides Roman-numeral reference.
nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong sequence: tiles reset with a dull knock. No lockout.

nodes.name: Moon-phase trapdoor
nodes.mechanic: hidden discovery (move rug) + observation + shape-matching dial code
nodes.input: Three rotary dials, each with eight embossed moon-phase shapes.
nodes.derivation: Triptych paintings: crow count (1/2/3) = dial index; moon shape in that painting = dial value. Waxing vs waning crescents/gibbous are mirrored shapes; exact orientation matters.
nodes.failure_behavior: Trapdoor stays shut. Dials keep position; no lockout.

nodes.name: Astrolabe star plate
nodes.input: Rotate pointer to one of six engraved star-pattern plates.
nodes.solution_fixed: plate-2 (Orion: three aligned belt stars with four shoulder/foot stars)
nodes.derivation: Workshop window sky shows Orion (belt prominent). Match the visible star pattern to plate-2. Recognizing Orion's Belt shortcuts it; pure dot-pattern matching also suffices.
nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong plate: drawer stays shut. No lockout.

nodes.name: Sun-and-moon cabinet
nodes.mechanic: item placement, dual-cue (alchemical symbol + physical shape fit)
nodes.input: Place one item in each of two shaped slots.
nodes.derivation: Alchemy: sun=gold, moon=silver. Redundant non-knowledge path: round ring physically fits round sun recess, crescent-stamped coin fits crescent recess; grimoire page B margin confirms.
nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong/swapped placement: item pops back out and returns to inventory. No loss, no lockout.

yields.state_semantics: Persistent latched flag; may be achieved BEFORE the shutter is ever opened -- order is irrelevant. Feeds derived condition cond-beam-at-alcove.

nodes.notes: VALIDATOR REQUIRED FIX 2 APPLIED: p09 no longer requires moonbeam-on. beam-at-alcove is the derived condition cond-beam-at-alcove (moonbeam-on AND mirror-at-detent-3), evaluated continuously and latching whenever both inputs hold, regardless of order. Developer: implement as a condition check, never an ordered event pair (see developer_notes D2). Playtest R4 (art): when the beam reaches detent-3 while the sliding shelf is still closed, render a bright blocked-light spot ON the shelf face so the beat reads as 'blocked, look here', not 'bugged'.

nodes.notes: VALIDATOR ADVISORY + PLAYTEST R1 APPLIED: the terminal-refusal grammar (crow snaps once, turns its back, guards its wing; identical pose on every repeat, no escalation) covers BOTH reaching into the cage AND offering any inventory item at the brass feed cup -- the 'feed the crow' theory must die fast, not read as 'wrong food, keep trying'. See clu-crow-refusal and developer_notes D3/D4. The draught mis-pour case specifically remains governed by D1.

nodes.name: File silver shavings
nodes.location: anywhere (inventory combination); workbench close-up also accepts it
clues: clu-recipe-page (crescent-metal filed pictogram); spoon bowl is stamped with the same crescent hallmark as the coin, identifying it as silver
nodes.notes: Spoon is not consumed until a successful brew completes; re-filing is impossible only after the draught exists (no longer needed).

nodes.name: Brew the Unbinding Draught
nodes.mechanic: procedural apparatus puzzle with fixed parameters; ingredient order-free
nodes.input: Set flame stage; add ingredients in ANY order; stir with ladle (direction + count); release ladle to resolve.
nodes.flame_mechanics: Floor bellows pump raises stage; stages cycle 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1. Current stage shown by flame height AND which embossed rim rune (I/II/III) has its ember channel lit.
nodes.derivation: clu-recipe-page: flame pictogram + III; spiral with CCW arrowhead and five dots; three ingredient pictograms.

yields.state: draught-ready (cauldron liquid takes a pearlescent sheen with a slow spiral surface pattern -- pattern, not color, is the success cue)

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong stir direction/count or wrong flame at resolve: gray fizzle puff, all three ingredients float to the surface intact and auto-return to inventory, cauldron reverts to water. Infinitely retryable; nothing is consumed on failure.
nodes.notes: Playtest R3 (art/dev requirement): the recipe page's CCW spiral and the in-scene cauldron view must be orientation-consistent (both read top-down, same handedness), and the ladle's stir-direction affordance must make CW vs CCW unmistakable from the actual camera angle.

nodes.name: Bottle the draught
nodes.input: Use empty phial on ready cauldron.
nodes.notes: Cauldron remains draught-ready after filling; refills possible. This refill invariant is load-bearing for the feed-cup mis-pour case (developer_notes D1).

nodes.name: Feed the door
nodes.input: Pour phial into the crow's-beak rune basin on the door.
clues: basin sits directly over the vine-wrapped bolt; if crow is freed, it perches on the door lintel above the basin (silent nudge)

yields.state: door-unsealed (thorn-vines wither and crumble off the bolt)

nodes.notes: The rune basin is the ONLY pour target that advances state. See developer_notes D1 for the brass feed cup mis-pour case.

yields.beat: the crow flies out over the player's shoulder into the moonlit woods

solve_path_notes.structure: Two parallel mid-game branches after z1: WORKSHOP branch (p01 -> p03 -> p04) and CELLAR branch (p02 -> p06 -> p07; spoon; cage key). They cross-link twice: crank (workshop) is needed for the cellar light shaft; file (workshop) is needed with the cellar spoon. Any interleaving that satisfies the requirement edges is valid.
example_ordering_C_mirror_first: p09 (mirror set to detent-3 BEFORE the shutter ever opens)
p08 (cond-beam-at-alcove latches here; mirror was already set)
solve_path_notes.state_model: All progression stored as satisfied-requirement flags (zone unlocked, item held, state on) plus derived boolean conditions (see derived_conditions); never as step sequences. cond-beam-at-alcove is the canonical example: an AND over two latched states, order-free by construction (ordering C exercises the mirror-first path). Ingredient-add order in p14 is explicitly order-free; only stir direction/count and flame stage are parameterized.
solve_path_notes.revision_note: Validator required fix 1 applied: ordering A previously listed p04 before its prerequisite p05 and omitted the poker/spoon pickups; both orderings now include all free pickups (Validator's proposed correction of A confirmed by Designer).

developer_notes.topic: Brass feed cup mis-pour of the DRAUGHT (Validator advisory A3) -- RESOLVED 2026-07-04: user chose option (a) BLOCK at the style checkpoint. Implement (a), reusing the D4 refusal grammar; option (b) text retained for context only.
developer_notes.note: The brass feed cup on the crow cage is a plausible mis-pour target for itm-phial-draught. Developer must implement exactly ONE of: (a) BLOCK the pour -- phial-on-cup plays a small crow head-shake and the phial returns to inventory unspent (preferred: zero state churn); or (b) ALLOW it -- draught is spent, cup shows a filled state, and the player refills the phial at the still-draught-ready cauldron (the p15 refill invariant is load-bearing in this case). Either choice is soft-lock-free; do not ship any third behavior. This note governs the DRAUGHT specifically; all other offered items follow D4.

Implement beam-at-alcove strictly as the derived condition defined in derived_conditions: re-evaluate on every change to moonbeam-on or mirror-at-detent-3. Never gate it on the order in which those two were achieved.

The reach-into-cage refusal is terminal in tone (see clu-crow-refusal): same closed-off pose on every repeat, no escalation, no randomized variation that could read as progress toward grabbing a feather.

ANY inventory item offered/dragged onto the brass feed cup (herbs cannot be taken, but e.g. blossom, shavings, paste, feather, coin, ring, keys, spoon, poker) triggers the SAME terminal-refusal grammar as the cage reach: crow snaps once, turns its back, guards its wing; identical pose on every repeat, no escalation; the offered item returns to inventory unspent. There must be NO neutral 'item pops back' response at the cup -- neutrality reads as 'wrong food, keep trying' and sustains the false feeding theory. EXCEPTION: itm-phial-draught follows D1 (if D1 option (a) is chosen, its refusal should reuse this same grammar for consistency).

The XII cuckoo-crow pop fires ONCE per save file: first time the hands are set to XII, the carved toy crow pops briefly with a dry wooden clack, then retreats. Every subsequent XII setting produces the SPENT state: the little door hangs ajar, the toy lies tipped over on a visibly limp/broken spring, no motion, no sound beyond a faint creak. The one-shot flag is a persistent cosmetic latch (saved; never gates progression). The toy must read as a crude carved, paint-chipped TOY -- round body, painted dot eyes -- clearly distinct from the live crow's silhouette so it does not teach 'the clock matters to the crow'. The Roman-numeral ring remains fully readable in all clock states (it is the in-room numeral reference for p01).

red_herrings.design: Bent, plain-bit key by the door. Tempts use on the front door and cage. Fairness valve: close-up shows the bit is snapped and plain; cage keyhole is visibly star-shaped.

Ready-made potions tempt a shortcut (pour one in the door basin). Bottles are inspectable but stoppered with fused wax; pictogram labels depict unrelated effects (sleep, frost, growth). Differentiated by bottle SHAPE and label pictogram, never by liquid color alone.

Hands are movable; the FIRST XII setting pops a crude carved toy crow once (dry wooden clack, charm beat, no reward); every later XII shows the spent state -- door ajar, toy tipped on a limp broken spring, inert. De-escalated per Playtest R2 so it reads as flavor, not signal; the toy is paint-chipped and round-bodied, clearly NOT the live crow. Not pure noise: the numeral ring is the in-room Roman-numeral reference for p01, so time spent here still pays forward.

Not an item, but the level's biggest theory magnet (Playtest F1): the cup invites a 'feed the crow to get the feather' theory. Defused per R1: every offered item gets the crow's terminal refusal (see D4), so the theory dies on first contact instead of sustaining a food hunt.

Two decoy spreads (a zodiac wheel; an anatomical bird diagram) invite over-reading. Neither encodes anything; the bird diagram softly foreshadows the crow's role. (Validator A4: the zodiac wheel shares a star theme with the astrolabe -- time-cost only; playtest confirmed ~3-4 min, fair. Keep the wheel visually non-systematic: no highlighted constellation.)

anti_softlock_invariants: No consumable is destroyed by a failed attempt anywhere (p14 returns all ingredients on failure; p04 rejects wrong placements back to inventory; feed-cup offers return the item unspent per D4).
itm-poker, itm-file, itm-crank, mirror, winch, bellows, ladle, mortar are reusable and never consumed.
moonbeam-on and mirror-at-detent-3 are persistent latched states (no timers); cond-beam-at-alcove is a derived AND over them, true whenever both hold regardless of achievement order.
Locks (p01, p02, p03) have unlimited attempts, no lockout, dials retain position.
The crow cannot be interacted with harmfully; feather is granted exactly once and cannot be lost (it CAN be added to the cauldron anytime; failed brews return it).
itm-phial-draught can be refilled from the still-ready cauldron (p15 note); this covers the feed-cup mis-pour case if Developer chooses allow-behavior (developer_notes D1).
The clock's one-shot cuckoo pop (D5) is purely cosmetic and never gates progression; spending it changes nothing solvable.

colorblind_safety: Moon phases: pure silhouette shapes, no color reliance.
Element runes: distinct geometric glyphs (triangles/bars), paired with pictograms.
Gold ring vs silver coin: shape (round band vs crescent-stamped disc) + slot shape fit + hallmark stamps; never metal color alone.
Flame stages: height + which embossed numeral rune's ember channel is lit; never flame color alone.
Brew success: spiral surface PATTERN + pearlescent sheen animation, not a color change alone.
Potion-shelf red herrings: distinct bottle shapes + pictogram labels, not liquid color.
